stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रद्युम्नो रौक्मिणेयः स खलु तव कला शम्बरेणाहृतस्तं
हत्वा रत्या सहाप्तो निजपुरमहरद्रुक्मिकन्यां च धन्याम् ।
तत्पुत्रोऽथानिरुद्धो गुणनिधिरवहद्रोचनां रुक्मिपौत्रीं
तत्रोद्वाहे गतस्त्वं न्यवधि मुसलिना रुक्म्यपि द्यूतवैरात् ॥ ८२-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Pradyumna, Rukmini's son was an aspect of Krishna. He was kidnapped by Shambara but later killed by Pradyumna. He returned to Dwaraka with his wife Rati. He also married the fortunate daughter of Rukmi. His virtuous son Aniruddha married Rochanaa, the grand daughter of Rukmi & Krishna attended the wedding. During a quarrel in the game of dice, Rukmi was killed by Balaraam.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pradyumno raukmiṇeyaḥ sa khalu tava kalā śambareṇāhṛtastaṃ
hatvā ratyā sahāpto nijapuramaharadrukmikanyāṃ ca dhanyām |
tatputro’thāniruddho guṇanidhiravahadrocanāṃ rukmipautrīṃ
tatrodvāhe gatastvaṃ nyavadhi musalinā rukmyapi dyūtavairāt || 82-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
बाणस्य सा बलिसुतस्य सहस्रबाहो-
-र्माहेश्वरस्य महिता दुहिता किलोषा ।
त्वत्पौत्रमेनमनिरुद्धमदृष्टपूर्वं
स्वप्नेऽनुभूय भगवन् विरहातुराऽभूत् ॥ ८२-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: MahaBali's son Baanasuran was a devotee of Shiva and had a thousand arms. His daughter Ushai had not seen Bhagwan’s grandson Aniruddha before. But she met him in her dreams and suffered from separation of him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bāṇasya sā balisutasya sahasrabāho-
-rmāheśvarasya mahitā duhitā kiloṣā |
tvatpautramenamaniruddhamadṛṣṭapūrvaṃ
svapne’nubhūya bhagavan virahāturā’bhūt || 82-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
योगिन्यतीव कुशला खलु चित्रलेखा
तस्याः सखी विलिखती तरुणानशेषान् ।
तत्रानिरुद्धमुषया विदितं निशाया-
-मानेष्ट योगबलतो भवतो निकेतात् ॥ ८२-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Her friend Chitralekha who was with yogic powers, drew several portraits of young men. Ushai identified Aniruddha and Chitralekha using her yogic powers, brought him from Dwaraka palace during night.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yoginyatīva kuśalā khalu citralekhā
tasyāḥ sakhī vilikhatī taruṇānaśeṣān |
tatrāniruddhamuṣayā viditaṃ niśāyā-
-māneṣṭa yogabalato bhavato niketāt || 82-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कन्यापुरे दयितया सुखमारमन्तं
चैनं कथञ्चन बबन्धुषि शर्वबन्धौ ।
श्रीनारदोक्ततदुदन्तदुरन्तरोषै-
-स्त्वं तस्य शोणितपुरं यदुभिर्न्यरुन्धाः ॥ ८२-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Aniruddha was happily spending time with Ushai in her private room. Shivaa's devotee Baanasuran came to know this and tied him up. Krishna heard this news through Sri Narada and immediately went to Shonitapura in anger and attacked Baanasuran with the help of Yadavas.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kanyāpure dayitayā sukhamāramantaṃ
cainaṃ kathañcana babandhuṣi śarvabandhau |
śrīnāradoktatadudantadurantaroṣai-
-stvaṃ tasya śoṇitapuraṃ yadubhirnyarundhāḥ || 82-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पुरीपालः शैलप्रियदुहितृनाथोऽस्य भगवान्
समं भूतव्रातैर्यदुबलमशङ्कं निरुरुधे ।
महाप्राणो बाणो झटिति युयुधानेन युयुधे
गुहः प्रद्युम्नेन त्वमपि पुरहन्त्रा जघटिषे ॥ ८२-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Lord Shiva was protecting the city of his bhakta due to his affection. Lord Shiva with his Bhootaganaas army blocked the Yadavas army. Baanasuran fought with Saathyaki, Skanda with Pradyumna and Krishna with Parameshwara in this battle.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
purīpālaḥ śailapriyaduhitṛnātho’sya bhagavān
samaṃ bhūtavrātairyadubalamaśaṅkaṃ nirurudhe |
mahāprāṇo bāṇo jhaṭiti yuyudhānena yuyudhe
guhaḥ pradyumnena tvamapi purahantrā jaghaṭiṣe || 82-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
निरुद्धाशेषास्त्रे मुमुहुषि तवास्त्रेण गिरिशे
द्रुता भूता भीताः प्रमथकुलवीराः प्रमथिताः ।
परास्कन्दत् स्कन्दः कुसुमशरबाणैश्च सचिवः
स कुम्भाण्डो भाण्डं नवमिव बलेनाशु बिभिदे ॥ ८२-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna blocked all the asthrams of Lord Shiva and defeated him. Shiva's army of Bhoothaganaas ran away in fear. Pradhyumna won over Skanda and Balarama killed Banasura's minister Kumbapandan easily, like breaking a pot.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
niruddhāśeṣāstre mumuhuṣi tavāstreṇa giriśe
drutā bhūtā bhītāḥ pramathakulavīrāḥ pramathitāḥ |
parāskandat skandaḥ kusumaśarabāṇaiśca sacivaḥ
sa kumbhāṇḍo bhāṇḍaṃ navamiva balenāśu bibhide || 82-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
चापानां पञ्चशत्या प्रसभमुपगते छिन्नचापेऽथ बाणे
व्यर्थे याते समेतो ज्वरपतिरशनैरज्वरि त्वज्ज्वरेण ।
ज्ञानी स्तुत्वाथ दत्त्वा तव चरितजुषां विज्वरं स ज्वरोऽगात्
प्रायोऽन्तर्ज्ञानवन्तोऽपि च बहुतमसा रौद्रचेष्टा हि रौद्राः ॥ ८२-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Baanasuran then attacked Krishna with 500 bow and arrow in his 1000 arms. Krishna broke all the bows and arrows and his chariot & defeated Baanasuran. Then the Shaiva fever, head of all fevers fought with Vaishnava fever.
Later understanding the significance of Bhagwan Krishna, requested that whoever reads this story should be protected from any kind of fever. Rudra's followers are good natured and knowledgeable but sometimes due to thamo guna they became arrogant.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
cāpānāṃ pañcaśatyā prasabhamupagate chinnacāpe’tha bāṇe
vyarthe yāte sameto jvarapatiraśanairajvari tvajjvareṇa |
jñānī stutvātha dattvā tava caritajuṣāṃ vijvaraṃ sa jvaro’gāt
prāyo’ntarjñānavanto’pi ca bahutamasā raudraceṣṭā hi raudrāḥ || 82-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
बाणं नानायुधोग्रं पुनरभिपतितं दर्पदोषाद्वितन्वन्
निर्लूनाशेषदोषं सपदि बुबुधुषा शङ्करेणोपगीतः ।
तद्वाचा शिष्टबाहुद्वितयमुभयतो निर्भयं तत्प्रियं तं
मुक्त्वा तद्दत्तमानो निजपुरमगमः सानिरुद्धः सहोषः ॥ ८२-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Baanasuran again attacked ferociously with many weapons. Krishna cut all his arms. Shiva realised Bhagwan’s greatness & on his request, Krishna granted Baanasuran two arms and spared him from the fear of death. Pleased with Krishna's mercy, Baanasuran gave lot of wealth and Krishna returned to Dwaraka with Aniruddha and Ushai.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bāṇaṃ nānāyudhograṃ punarabhipatitaṃ darpadoṣādvitanvan
nirlūnāśeṣadoṣaṃ sapadi bubudhuṣā śaṅkareṇopagītaḥ |
tadvācā śiṣṭabāhudvitayamubhayato nirbhayaṃ tatpriyaṃ taṃ
muktvā taddattamāno nijapuramagamaḥ sāniruddhaḥ sahoṣaḥ || 82-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मुहुस्तावच्छक्रं वरुणमजयो नन्दहरणे
यमं बालानीतौ दवदहनपानेऽनिलसखम् ।
विधिं वत्सस्तेये गिरिशमिह बाणस्य समरे
विभो विश्वोत्कर्षी तदयमवतारो जयति ते ॥ ८२-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Bhagwan won over Indra many times, lifted Govardhana hills, brought Parijata tree from Devaloka. (Dasakam 62-64)
HE won over Varuna when he took Nandagopan. (Dasakam 64)
HE won over Yama when HE went to save HIS Guru's son from jaws of death. (Dasakam 76)
HE drank the forest fire and won over Agni who was friend to Vaayu God. (Dasakam 58)
Krishna won over Brahma when he hid the cows. (Dasakam 52)
And now Bhagwan’s incarnation of winning over Lord Shiva in Baanasuran battle is the best of all. (Dasakam 82)
stanzas.stanza_roman:
muhustāvacchakraṃ varuṇamajayo nandaharaṇe
yamaṃ bālānītau davadahanapāne’nilasakham |
vidhiṃ vatsasteye giriśamiha bāṇasya samare
vibho viśvotkarṣī tadayamavatāro jayati te || 82-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
द्विजरुषा कृकलासवपुर्धरं
नृगनृपं त्रिदिवालयमापयन् ।
निजजने द्विजभक्तिमनुत्तमा-
-मुपदिशन् पवनेश्वर पाहि माम् ॥ ८२-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Nruga became a chameleon due to a brahmin's curse and Krishna relieved him and sent him to Swargaloka. Krishna instructed devotees to give supreme respect to the holy Brahmins. Bhattathiri requested Lord Guruvayoorappan to protect him from his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dvijaruṣā kṛkalāsavapurdharaṃ
nṛganṛpaṃ tridivālayamāpayan |
nijajane dvijabhaktimanuttamā-
-mupadiśan pavaneśvara pāhi mām || 82-10 ||
